question.problem: The function $f(x)=\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x-k)$ has an inverse function given by ${f}^{-1}(x)=\frac{{e}^{x}-9}{3}.$ What is the value of $k?$
question.worked_solution:
To find ${f}^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x-k)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(3y-k).\end{aligned}
$$

We make $y$ the subject of the equation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(3y-k) \\ {e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡(3y-k)} & ={e}^{x} \\ 3y-k & ={e}^{x} \\ 3y & ={e}^{x}+k \\ y & =\frac{{e}^{x}+k}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the inverse function is ${f}^{-1}(x)=\frac{{e}^{x}+k}{3}.$ 

Comparing our answer with the given expression, we conclude that $k=-9.$
